description: Volvariella volvacea, the paddy straw mushroom, is a warm-climate species widely cultivated across Southeast and East Asia on rice straw and other plant substrates. It is harvested mostly in its young, egg-like button stage, enclosed in a sac-like volva, and is a major commercial mushroom in tropical regions.
edibilityNotes: Edible and popular when cooked; harvested young in the volva-enclosed "egg" stage. CRITICAL SAFETY WARNING: in its button stage the paddy straw mushroom, enclosed in a basal volva, closely resembles the unexpanded "egg" stage of deadly Amanita species (death cap Amanita phalloides, destroying angels Amanita virosa / A. bisporigera), and such confusion has caused fatal poisonings. Distinguishing features: Volvariella has a PINK to salmon spore print and pink mature gills and NO stem ring (annulus), whereas deadly Amanita have a WHITE spore print, white gills, and usually a ring. Spore print and gill colour are not visible in the unopened button, so wild buttons should never be eaten. Best practice is to rely only on cultivated material; do not gather wild specimens unless an expert confirms identity.
distribution: Native to and cultivated throughout tropical and subtropical Asia, and grown commercially in warm regions worldwide.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Amanita phalloides
dangerousLookalikes.note: Death cap; deadly. Has a WHITE spore print, white gills, and a ring (annulus) on the stem. The button/egg stage and volva resemble young Volvariella, but Volvariella has a pink spore print, pink mature gills, and no ring. These features are not visible in the unopened button, so wild buttons must never be eaten.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Amanita virosa
dangerousLookalikes.note: Destroying angel; deadly. White overall with a white spore print, white gills, and a stem ring. Distinguished from paddy straw by Volvariella's pink spore print and gills and the absence of a ring.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Amanita bisporigera
dangerousLookalikes.note: Destroying angel (North American); deadly. All white with a white spore print, white gills, a stem ring, and a basal volva that can mimic a young Volvariella egg. Lacks the pink spores/gills of paddy straw.
